summary:
We developed TerraPhase, an interactive web platform that makes satellite evidence easier to explore and understand. Users select study sites on a globe to investigate forest disturbance, drought, floods, landslides, volcanic eruptions, and earthquakes. The platform brings together NASA–ISRO NISAR and Sentinel observations, rainfall records, terrain views, and independent reference data.

TerraPhase addresses the challenge of turning complex Earth observations into useful information. Users can compare imagery across dates, inspect mapped changes, and generate AI-assisted reports explaining observations, possible causes, uncertainties, and recommended checks. Selected cases include historically evaluated risk outlooks, with results displayed directly on maps. Source dates, measurement units, and evidence limitations remain visible so users can distinguish observations from estimates.

This matters because environmental change can threaten ecosystems, livelihoods, and communities. By bringing scattered evidence into one accessible workspace, TerraPhase helps researchers, land managers, and decision-makers identify areas needing attention and prioritize follow-up investigation.
details:
TerraPhase turns complex satellite observations into an interactive environmental investigation. Instead of starting with large scientific files, users begin with a globe. They choose a study site and explore evidence of forest disturbance, drought, flooding, landslides, volcanic activity, or earthquakes.

*How it works*

The platform brings together NASA–ISRO NISAR radar observations, Sentinel imagery, rainfall records, elevation data, and independent reference sources. Each study uses evidence appropriate to the event: drought comparisons place radar imagery alongside seasonal rainfall anomalies, while forest comparisons include vegetation references and candidate disturbance areas. Hazard studies add relevant layers, such as mapped surface water or radar-derived ground displacement.

Users can compare observations across dates, zoom into imagery, select areas, and explore terrain views where available. AI-assisted reports explain the evidence, possible causes, uncertainties, and recommended verification. Selected studies also provide historically evaluated outlooks; the river example includes a historical replay rather than a live warning.

*Benefits and intended impact*

TerraPhase reduces the effort needed to move between separate datasets and understand what they show. It helps researchers, land managers, students, and decision-makers identify areas that deserve closer investigation and communicate their findings. Its intended impact is better-informed environmental monitoring and follow-up, supported by traceable evidence.

*Tools and development*

We used Python for scientific processing, including *h5py, NumPy, Rasterio/GDAL, and Pillow* to read, align, process, and render radar data. *FastAPI* serves the native-resolution imagery backend. The interface uses *JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and browser-based mapping and graphics, with Node.js supporting development and packaging. **Scikit-learn* supports selected outlook models, the *OpenAI API* powers assisted interpretation, and *GitHub* supports team collaboration.

*Creativity and team considerations*

Our creative contribution is connecting geographic discovery, scientific imagery, environmental context, and understandable explanations in one workflow. We considered data compatibility, spatial resolution, seasonal variation, missing observations, accessibility, and model evaluation. Crucially, TerraPhase distinguishes radar backscatter from soil moisture, observed change from its possible cause, and experimental outlooks from established warnings. Sources, dates, units, and provisional evidence remain visible throughout.
